literature.headline_zh: 人肠道病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期人肠道病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: ATF3 在 EV-A71 感染期间显着上调并易位到细胞质,在细胞质中与病毒 5'UTR 相互作用并促进 基因组 RNA 复制。此外,ATF3 的核定位信号 (NLS) 通过与病毒 基因组 结合而促进了这一过程。 [10.1016/j.biocel.2026.107054]
CVA10 感染儿童的病程(9.5 天)明显长于 CVA16 感染儿童(8.0 天,P = 0.012)。CVA16 感染与更多症状病例(尤其是更高的皮疹 发病率)以及就医行为增加相关。 [10.1186/s12887-026-07700-x]
DDX58 敲除显着减少了 EV-A71 复制,病毒 RNA 水平和 VP1 蛋白表达降低表明了这一点。此外,关键 抗病毒药物 信号分子(包括 IRF3、IRF7 和 CXCL-10)的表达在感染后 24 小时显示短暂增加,随后在 36 小时下降。一致地,IFN-α和IFN-β水平表现出类似的时间依赖性模式,早期升高,随后降低。 [10.21203/rs.3.rs-11209151/v1]
病例报告证实EV-D68可诱发原本健康的学龄儿童塑性支气管炎,导致气道阻塞、呼吸窘迫,甚至呼吸衰竭。经过 16 天的综合 治疗(包括反复支气管镜灌洗、静脉注射免疫球蛋白和甲泼尼龙)后,患者的病情有所改善,这表明积极的多模式干预可能是获得良好结果的关键。研究结果还支持以下观点:EV-D68 感染是儿童塑料性支气管炎或重症肺炎的潜在病因。 [PMCID:PMC13719561]
在 1,974 例疑似手足口病病例中,1,179 例(59.7%)病毒 RNA(VR)阳性,83 例(VR 阳性病例的 7%)检测到 CV-A6。感染主要发生在1-2岁的男性儿童中。 [10.51403/0868-2836/2026/3630]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: ATF3 was significantly upregulated during EV-A71 infection and translocated to the cytoplasm, where it interacted with the viral 5'UTR and promoted genome RNA replication. Additionally, the nuclear localization signal (NLS) of ATF3 contributed to this process by binding to the viral genome. [10.1016/j.biocel.2026.107054]

CVA10-infected children had a significantly longer duration (9.5 days) than those with CVA16 (8.0 days, P = 0.012). CVA16 infection correlated with more symptomatic cases, especially higher rash incidence, and increased healthcare-seeking behavior. [10.1186/s12887-026-07700-x]

DDX58 knockdown significantly reduced EV-A71 replication, as indicated by decreased viral RNA levels and VP1 protein expression. Additionally, the expression of key antiviral signaling molecules, including IRF3, IRF7, and CXCL-10, showed a transient increase at 24 hours post-infection, followed by a decline at 36 hours. [10.21203/rs.3.rs-11209151/v1]

The case report confirms that EV-D68 can induce plastic bronchitis in previously healthy school-aged children, leading to airway obstruction, respiratory distress, and even respiratory failure. [PMCID:PMC13719561]

Out of 1,974 suspected HFMD cases, 1,179 (59.7%) were positive for viral RNA (VR), and CV-A6 was detected in 83 cases (7% of VR-positive cases). The infection was predominantly in male children aged 1-2 years. [10.51403/0868-2836/2026/3630]

papers.title: Enterovirus D68 in Europe, 2025: continent-wide predominance of subclade A2/D and shift from pediatric to adult cases
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) has predominantly caused infections in children, and detected cases have mainly been infected by subclade B3. In 2025, however, a substantial number of infections in adults was noted. Aim To detail the molecular epidemiology of the 2025 season in Europe. Methods Case and sequencing data was collected from members in the European Non-Polio Enterovirus Network (ENPEN). The participating sites included both clinical and public health laboratories. Results Data was collected from 13 countries at 23 sites. There were 187 clinical cases infected with EV-D68 and 127 detections in wastewater. Age data were available for 76% (143/187), among which 90 cases were adults. VP1-based genotyping showed subclade A2/D to predominate in all age groups and across all participating countries, as well as in the sewage sampling performed at one site. Two interclade recombinant sequences were detected among 22 whole genome sequences. Conclusion The observed shift towards adult cases and subclade A2/D predominance warrants continued monitoring to determine whether this represents a sustained epidemiological change. The detection of interclade recombinant variants highlights a need to supplement regular VP1-based genotyping with whole-genome sequencing.

papers.title: Viral shedding and clinical differences in hand, foot and mouth disease associated with coxsackievirus A16 and coxsackievirus A10
papers.abstract: Hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) remains a major and persistent public health challenge in China and across many parts of Asia. Following widespread implementation of enterovirus A71 vaccination in China, coxsackievirus A10 (CVA10) and coxsackievirus A16 (CVA16) have emerged as the dominant serotypes associated with outbreaks in children. To investigate the viral shedding duration and clinical differences of CVA10 and CVA16 in HFMD outbreaks in Jiangsu Province, and to generate evidence for optimizing case management and outbreak control. In 2024, a total of 63 HFMD cases were prospectively followed daily to monitor symptom progression. Pharyngeal swabs were collected once at symptom onset and on days 3, 7, 10, and 14 post-onset from cases and close contacts. All specimens were tested by RT-PCR for nucleic acid detection and serotype identification. CVA10-infected children had a significantly longer duration (9.5 days) than those with CVA16 (8.0 days, P = 0.012). CVA16 infection correlated with more symptomatic cases, especially higher rash incidence, and increased healthcare-seeking behavior. Viral load dropped sharply from days 1–4, and symptom duration was positively correlated with viral shedding duration in symptomatic children ( r = 0.33); 91.7% of children tested negative within 5 days after symptom resolution. This study suggests that symptom resolution may provide a potential reference for evaluating isolation strategies, early monitoring is critical due to rapid viral load decline, and symptom duration may serve as an indicator of viral RNA shedding duration. Given CVA10’s prolonged viral shedding and CVA16’s symptom-driven transmission, serotype-specific and tailored management strategies may be valuable for HFMD control. However, infectivity was not directly assessed, and these findings should be further validated using viral culture.

Following widespread implementation of enterovirus A71 vaccination in China, coxsackievirus A10 (CVA10) and coxsackievirus A16 (CVA16) have emerged as the dominant serotypes associated with outbreaks in children. To investigate the viral shedding duration and clinical differences of CVA10 and CVA16 in HFMD outbreaks in Jiangsu Province, and to generate evidence for optimizing case management and outbreak control. In 2024, a total of 63 HFMD cases were prospectively followed daily to monitor symptom progression. Pharyngeal swabs were collected once at symptom onset and on days 3, 7, 10, and 14 post-onset from cases and close contacts. All specimens were tested by RT-PCR for nucleic acid detection and serotype identification. CVA10-infected children had a significantly longer duration (9.5 days) than those with CVA16 (8.0 days, P = 0.012). CVA16 infection correlated with more symptomatic cases, especially higher rash incidence, and increased healthcare-seeking behavior. Viral load dropped sharply from days 1–4, and symptom duration was positively correlated with viral shedding duration in symptomatic children ( r = 0.33); 91.7% of children tested negative within 5 days after symptom resolution. This study suggests that symptom resolution may provide a potential reference for evaluating isolation strategies, early monitoring is critical due to rapid viral load decline, and symptom duration may serve as an indicator of viral RNA shedding duration. Given CVA10’s prolonged viral shedding and CVA16’s symptom-driven transmission, serotype-specific and tailored management strategies may be valuable for HFMD control. However, infectivity was not directly assessed, and these findings should be further validated using viral culture.

papers.title: Effects of DDX58 Gene Knockdown on EV-A71 Replication and Modulation of RIG-I–Mediated Antiviral
papers.abstract: Abstract Objective: The aim of this study was to investigate the role of DDX58 (RIG-I) in EV-A71 replication and its impact on RIG-I–mediated antiviral signaling responses. Methods: DDX58 knockdown was achieved using siRNA transfection in RD cells, followed by EV-A71 infection. Viral replication and host antiviral responses were assessed by qRT-PCR and Western blotting. The secretion of interferons (IFN-α and IFN-β) and CXCL-10 was measured by ELISA. Results: DDX58 knockdown significantly reduced EV-A71 replication, as indicated by decreased viral RNA levels and VP1 protein expression. Additionally, the expression of key antiviral signaling molecules, including IRF3, IRF7, and CXCL-10, showed a transient increase at 24 hours post-infection, followed by a decline at 36 hours. Consistently, IFN-α and IFN-β levels exhibited a similar time-dependent pattern, with early elevation and subsequent reduction. Conclusion: These findings suggest that DDX58 may exert a context- and time-dependent regulatory effect on EV-A71 replication and antiviral signaling. The observed transient activation of downstream pathways despite DDX58 knockdown indicates potential involvement of compensatory innate immune mechanisms. Further studies are required to elucidate the underlying molecular interactions.

Methods: DDX58 knockdown was achieved using siRNA transfection in RD cells, followed by EV-A71 infection. Viral replication and host antiviral responses were assessed by qRT-PCR and Western blotting. The secretion of interferons (IFN-α and IFN-β) and CXCL-10 was measured by ELISA. Results: DDX58 knockdown significantly reduced EV-A71 replication, as indicated by decreased viral RNA levels and VP1 protein expression. Additionally, the expression of key antiviral signaling molecules, including IRF3, IRF7, and CXCL-10, showed a transient increase at 24 hours post-infection, followed by a decline at 36 hours. Consistently, IFN-α and IFN-β levels exhibited a similar time-dependent pattern, with early elevation and subsequent reduction. Conclusion: These findings suggest that DDX58 may exert a context- and time-dependent regulatory effect on EV-A71 replication and antiviral signaling. The observed transient activation of downstream pathways despite DDX58 knockdown indicates potential involvement of compensatory innate immune mechanisms. Further studies are required to elucidate the underlying molecular interactions.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在调查 DDX58 (RIG-I) 在 EV-A71 复制中的作用及其对 RIG-I 介导的 抗病毒药物 信号反应的影响。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 通过在 RD 细胞中转染 siRNA,然后感染 EV-A71,实现了 DDX58 敲低。该研究的重点是评估该细胞模型中的病毒复制和 宿主 抗病毒药物 反应。
elements_zh.methods: 通过 qRT-PCR 和蛋白质印迹评估病毒复制和 宿主 抗病毒药物 反应。通过ELISA测定干扰素(IFN-α和IFN-β)和CXCL-10的分泌。
elements_zh.main_results: DDX58 敲除显着减少了 EV-A71 复制,病毒 RNA 水平和 VP1 蛋白表达降低表明了这一点。此外,关键 抗病毒药物 信号分子(包括 IRF3、IRF7 和 CXCL-10)的表达在感染后 24 小时显示短暂增加,随后在 36 小时下降。一致地,IFN-α和IFN-β水平表现出类似的时间依赖性模式,早期升高,随后降低。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现表明,DDX58 可能对 EV-A71 复制和 抗病毒药物 信号传导发挥上下文和时间依赖性调节作用。尽管 DDX58 被敲低,但观察到的下游通路的短暂激活表明补偿性先天免疫机制的潜在参与。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果提供了对 EV-A71 复制和 抗病毒药物 信号传导的分子机制的见解,这可以为未来针对 DDX58 或相关途径的治疗策略的研究提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于使用 RD 细胞的体外实验,可能无法完全代表体内条件。证据是中等的,因为它基于单一实验模型,不包括临床或流行病学数据。

papers.title: Enterovirus A71 upregulates and recruits host ATF3 to promote viral replication.
papers.abstract: To hijack cellular resources, certain viruses such as EV-A71, induce the shutoff of cellular transcription and translation systems globally for establishing infection. However, our previous studies have shown that the translation efficiency of series host proteins is upregulated during EV-A71 infection potentially, including activating transcription factor 3 (ATF3). Here, we validated in RD cells that ATF3 is mount up during EV-A71 infection significantly via increasing mRNA and cap-independent translation. Our findings highlight the critical role of ATF3 in EV-A71 replication: during EV-A71 infection, ATF3 trans-locates to the cytoplasm besides upregulated, where it interacts with the viral 5' untranslated region (5'UTR) and promotes the replication of viral genome RNA. Intriguingly, the nuclear localization signal (NLS) of ATF3 also contributes to this process, including binding to the viral genome and facilitating viral replication.
papers.journal: The international journal of biochemistry & cell biology

papers.title: Ferritin-displayed engineered sCAR1 nanoparticles as a receptor-decoy antiviral strategy against Coxsackievirus B-associated inflammation
papers.abstract: Coxsackievirus Group B (CVB) remains an important cause of severe disease in infants and young children, including viral myocarditis and meningitis, yet no licensed vaccine or virus-specific antiviral therapy is currently available. Here, we engineered soluble Coxsackievirus and adenovirus receptor (CAR) ectodomains and displayed the optimized receptor decoy on ferritin nanoparticles to generate a potent anti-CVB3 entry inhibitor. Wild-type soluble CAR ectodomains neutralized CVB3 but were limited by homodimerization and by residual binding to endogenous CAR/JAML, which was associated with dose-dependent mitogenic activity. Guided by structural information, we introduced mutations that abolished dimerization and CAR/JAML binding while preserving, and further improving, viral neutralization. Ferritin display of the optimized sCAR1 mutant enhanced multivalent presentation, systemic persistence, and tissue delivery. The resulting sCAR1 Mu+Ferritin nanoparticle achieved IC<sub>50</sub> values of 413 ng/mL in Vero cells and 140 ng/mL in SH-SY5Y cells. In neonatal BALB/c mice, prophylactic administration of sCAR1 Mu+Ferritin (200 μg, 6 h before challenge) conferred 68.75% protection against lethal CVB3 infection (10<sup>3.5</sup> CCID<sub>50</sub>), reduced viral burden in the liver, spleen, brain, and heart, and alleviated myocarditis and neuroinflammation without sustained cytokine activation. Cross-neutralizing activity against CVB1 further supports the breadth of this receptor-based platform. These findings identify ferritin-displayed engineered CAR nanoparticles as a safety-optimized and mutation-resilient antiviral strategy for CVB infections.

analysis.methods: The researchers engineered soluble CAR ectodomains, introduced mutations to abolish dimerization and CAR/JAML binding, and displayed the optimized receptor decoy on ferritin nanoparticles. The efficacy was assessed in Vero and SH-SY5Y cells and in neonatal BALB/c mice.

analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the use of a single CVB3 strain and the need for further validation in larger animal models and human clinical trials. The evidence strength is moderate due to the in vitro and in vivo experimental nature of the study.

papers.title_zh: 铁蛋白展示的工程 sCAR1 纳米颗粒作为受体诱饵 抗病毒药物 策略对抗柯萨奇病毒 B 相关炎症
papers.source_body_en: Coxsackievirus Group B (CVB) remains an important cause of severe disease in infants and young children, including viral myocarditis and meningitis, yet no licensed vaccine or virus-specific antiviral therapy is currently available. Here, we engineered soluble Coxsackievirus and adenovirus receptor (CAR) ectodomains and displayed the optimized receptor decoy on ferritin nanoparticles to generate a potent anti-CVB3 entry inhibitor. Wild-type soluble CAR ectodomains neutralized CVB3 but were limited by homodimerization and by residual binding to endogenous CAR/JAML, which was associated with dose-dependent mitogenic activity. Guided by structural information, we introduced mutations that abolished dimerization and CAR/JAML binding while preserving, and further improving, viral neutralization. Ferritin display of the optimized sCAR1 mutant enhanced multivalent presentation, systemic persistence, and tissue delivery. The resulting sCAR1 Mu+Ferritin nanoparticle achieved IC<sub>50</sub> values of 413 ng/mL in Vero cells and 140 ng/mL in SH-SY5Y cells. In neonatal BALB/c mice, prophylactic administration of sCAR1 Mu+Ferritin (200 μg, 6 h before challenge) conferred 68.75% protection against lethal CVB3 infection (10<sup>3.5</sup> CCID<sub>50</sub>), reduced viral burden in the liver, spleen, brain, and heart, and alleviated myocarditis and neuroinflammation without sustained cytokine activation. Cross-neutralizing activity against CVB1 further supports the breadth of this receptor-based platform. These findings identify ferritin-displayed engineered CAR nanoparticles as a safety-optimized and mutation-resilient antiviral strategy for CVB infections.
papers.abstract_zh: B 组柯萨奇病毒 (CVB) 仍然是婴儿和幼儿严重疾病的重要原因,包括病毒性心肌炎和脑膜炎,但目前尚无获得许可的 疫苗 或病毒特异性 抗病毒药物 疗法。在这里,我们设计了可溶性柯萨奇病毒和腺病毒受体 (CAR) 胞外域,并将优化的受体诱饵展示在铁蛋白纳米粒子上,以产生有效的抗 CVB3 进入抑制剂。野生型可溶性 CAR 胞外域中和了 CVB3,但受到同源二聚化和与内源 CAR/JAML 的残留结合的限制,这与剂量依赖性有丝分裂活性相关。在结构信息的指导下,我们引入了 突变,它消除了二聚化和 CAR/JAML 结合,同时保留并进一步改善了病毒中和作用。优化的 sCAR1 突变体的铁蛋白展示增强了多价呈递、全身持久性和组织递送。所得的sCAR1 Mu+铁蛋白纳米颗粒在Vero细胞中达到413ng/mL的IC<sub>50</sub>值,在SH-SY5Y细胞中达到140ng/mL。在新生 BALB/c 小鼠中,预防性施用 sCAR1 Mu+铁蛋白(200 μg,攻击前 6 小时)可提供 68.75% 的针对致死性 CVB3 感染 (10<sup>3.5</sup> CCID<sub>50</sub>) 的保护,减少肝脏、脾脏、大脑和心脏中的病毒负荷,并减轻心肌炎和神经炎症,而无需持续的细胞因子激活。针对 CVB1 的交叉中和活性进一步支持了这种基于受体的平台的广度。这些发现将铁蛋白展示的工程 CAR 纳米颗粒确定为针对 CVB 感染的安全优化且具有 突变 弹性的 抗病毒药物 策略。

papers.title: Detection of novel Echovirus 25 lineage from patients and sewage in Fukuoka in 2024
papers.abstract: Echovirus 25 (E25), belonging to the Enterovirus B species of viruses, is known to cause infectious gastroenteriris, aseptic meningitis, and acute flaccid paralysis. Our study aims to conduct enterovirus surveillance and subsequent molecular epidemiology investigations among patients and sewage samples in Fukuoka. In 2024, a total of ten and seven enteroviral strains were detected in 141 clinical specimens and 24 sewage samples, respectively. Among them, five E25 strains were identified, and phylogenetic analysis of VP1 region revealed that these strains constituted a distinct clade separated from previously reported E25 strains. Full-length genome sequences were determined using sequence-independent, single-primer amplification and next-generation sequencing. The five strains had sequence identities ranging from 99.0% to 99.9% among themselves. Through phylogenetic analysis, the five strains were classified as E25 on the basis of P1, and P1–3 sequences, and as E3 and E11 on the basis of P2–3 sequence. Furthermore, SimPlot and RDP4 analysis revealed a unique recombination event between the detected E25 strains and E3 in the region of the 2B gene, which is the non-structural region. These findings indicated the emergence of a novel E25 lineage in 2024, and underscore the importance of continued surveillance to monitor its evolution and circulation.

papers.title_zh: 2024 年福冈患者和污水中检测到新型埃可病毒 25 谱系
papers.source_body_en: Echovirus 25 (E25), belonging to the Enterovirus B species of viruses, is known to cause infectious gastroenteriris, aseptic meningitis, and acute flaccid paralysis. Our study aims to conduct enterovirus surveillance and subsequent molecular epidemiology investigations among patients and sewage samples in Fukuoka. In 2024, a total of ten and seven enteroviral strains were detected in 141 clinical specimens and 24 sewage samples, respectively. Among them, five E25 strains were identified, and phylogenetic analysis of VP1 region revealed that these strains constituted a distinct clade separated from previously reported E25 strains. Full-length genome sequences were determined using sequence-independent, single-primer amplification and next-generation sequencing. The five strains had sequence identities ranging from 99.0% to 99.9% among themselves. Through phylogenetic analysis, the five strains were classified as E25 on the basis of P1, and P1–3 sequences, and as E3 and E11 on the basis of P2–3 sequence. Furthermore, SimPlot and RDP4 analysis revealed a unique recombination event between the detected E25 strains and E3 in the region of the 2B gene, which is the non-structural region. These findings indicated the emergence of a novel E25 lineage in 2024, and underscore the importance of continued surveillance to monitor its evolution and circulation.

papers.title: Enterovirus A71 neuroinvasion: central nervous system entry, blood–brain barrier dynamics, and multistage constraints
papers.abstract: Enterovirus A71 (EV-A71) is an important cause of severe neurological complications of hand, foot, and mouth disease in children. Most infections remain confined to peripheral sites, whereas only a small proportion progress to central nervous system (CNS) disease, and the mechanisms underlying this transition remain incompletely understood. Here, we reappraise EV-A71 neuropathogenesis as a multistage process comprising peripheral replication, systemic dissemination, CNS entry, establishment of productive CNS infection, and subsequent tissue injury. This distinction is important because these events are mechanistically connected but not interchangeable. Current evidence supports both neurovascular and peripheral neural routes of CNS entry, although the nature and strength of the supporting evidence differ. Human-derived blood–brain barrier (BBB) models demonstrate that EV-A71 and virus-associated carriers can engage and cross neurovascular interfaces, whereas temporal studies in animals, perturbation of axonal transport, and compartmentalized neuronal models provide stronger causal support for retrograde axonal transport once the virus has accessed peripheral nerves. These findings establish mechanistic feasibility, but the timing, necessity, and relative contribution of each route during natural infection in children remain unresolved. We further emphasize that BBB crossing is not synonymous with BBB disruption, and that CNS entry does not necessarily result in productive CNS infection. On this basis, we propose a multistage progression-constraint model, in which progression to severe neurological disease requires EV-A71 to overcome distinct constraints imposed by tissue context, viral properties, and host factors at successive stages. This framework provides a testable explanation for why most infections remain peripheral while only a minority progress to severe neurological disease, and highlights the need for longitudinal clinical studies and directly comparable experimental models to identify where disease trajectories first diverge.

Most infections remain confined to peripheral sites, whereas only a small proportion progress to central nervous system (CNS) disease, and the mechanisms underlying this transition remain incompletely understood. Here, we reappraise EV-A71 neuropathogenesis as a multistage process comprising peripheral replication, systemic dissemination, CNS entry, establishment of productive CNS infection, and subsequent tissue injury. This distinction is important because these events are mechanistically connected but not interchangeable. Current evidence supports both neurovascular and peripheral neural routes of CNS entry, although the nature and strength of the supporting evidence differ. Human-derived blood–brain barrier (BBB) models demonstrate that EV-A71 and virus-associated carriers can engage and cross neurovascular interfaces, whereas temporal studies in animals, perturbation of axonal transport, and compartmentalized neuronal models provide stronger causal support for retrograde axonal transport once the virus has accessed peripheral nerves. These findings establish mechanistic feasibility, but the timing, necessity, and relative contribution of each route during natural infection in children remain unresolved. We further emphasize that BBB crossing is not synonymous with BBB disruption, and that CNS entry does not necessarily result in productive CNS infection. On this basis, we propose a multistage progression-constraint model, in which progression to severe neurological disease requires EV-A71 to overcome distinct constraints imposed by tissue context, viral properties, and host factors at successive stages. This framework provides a testable explanation for why most infections remain peripheral while only a minority progress to severe neurological disease, and highlights the need for longitudinal clinical studies and directly comparable experimental models to identify where disease trajectories first diverge.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the mechanisms of Enterovirus A71 (EV-A71) neuroinvasion, focusing on how it transitions from peripheral sites to the central nervous system (CNS) in children. The research highlights the multistage process of EV-A71 neuropathogenesis, including peripheral replication, systemic dissemination, CNS entry, and tissue injury. It identifies both neurovascular and peripheral neural routes as potential pathways for CNS entry, though the evidence supporting these routes varies in strength. The study emphasizes that BBB crossing does not equate to BBB disruption and that CNS entry may not always lead to productive infection. It proposes a multistage progression-constraint model to explain why most infections remain peripheral while only a minority progress to severe neurological disease. The findings suggest the need for longitudinal clinical studies and experimental models to better understand the divergence of disease trajectories. However, the study acknowledges unresolved questions about the timing and relative contribution of each route during natural infection.

papers.abstract_zh: 肠道病毒A71(EV-A71)是导致儿童手足口病严重神经并发症的重要原因。大多数感染仍然局限于外周部位,而只有一小部分感染进展为中枢神经系统(CNS)疾病,并且这种转变背后的机制仍不完全清楚。在这里,我们重新评估 EV-A71 神经发病机制为一个多阶段过程,包括外周复制、全身传播、进入中枢神经系统、产生有效中枢神经系统感染和随后的组织损伤。这种区别很重要,因为这些事件在机械上是相关的,但不可互换。目前的证据支持神经血管和周围神经途径进入中枢神经系统,尽管支持证据的性质和强度有所不同。人源性血脑屏障(BBB)模型表明,EV-A71和病毒相关载体可以接触并穿过神经血管界面,而动物的时间研究、轴突运输的扰动和区室化神经元模型为病毒进入周围神经后的逆行轴突运输提供了更强的因果支持。这些发现确立了机制上的可行性,但儿童自然感染过程中每种途径的时间、必要性和相对贡献仍未解决。我们进一步强调,血脑屏障穿越并不等同于血脑屏障破坏,并且中枢神经系统进入并不一定会导致有效的中枢神经系统感染。在此基础上,我们提出了一个多阶段进展约束模型,其中进展为严重神经系统疾病需要 EV-A71 克服连续阶段的组织背景、病毒特性和 宿主 因素所施加的不同约束。该框架为为什么大多数感染仍处于外围状态而只有少数进展为严重神经系统疾病提供了可测试的解释,并强调需要进行纵向临床研究和直接可比较的实验模型来确定疾病轨迹首先出现分歧的地方。

source_records.title: Enterovirus D68 infection causing plastic bronchitis and severe pneumonia: a case report and literature review

papers.full_text: AbstractBackgroundPlastic bronchitis (PB) is a rare disease characterized by the formation of tree-like or tubular mucus plugs within the bronchi, which can lead to severe airway obstruction and respiratory failure, potentially becoming life-threatening if diagnosis and treatment are delayed. Enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) is a common pathogen that causes acute respiratory infections in children,which can lead to wheezing, acute flaccid myelitis, and even respiratory failure. Nevertheless, a direct association between EV-D68 infection and plastic bronchitis has not been previously reported. As the first documented case, this report establishes the association between EV-D68 and plastic bronchitis, thereby expanding the clinical spectrum of EV-D68.MethodsWe report a case of plastic bronchitis and severe pneumonia caused by Enterovirus D68 infection. To identify additional cases and elucidate the clinical characteristics of this condition, a systematic literature search was conducted using PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science databases for the period from January 2006 to June 2026. The search strategy employed the following keywords: “Enterovirus D68” “plastic bronchitis” and “severe pneumonia”.Case descriptionThis case involved an 11-year-old girl with previously good health. Chief complaints: cough and wheezing for 1 day, chest pain for half a day. Chest CT showed patchy increased-density opacities in the left upper loben with reduced left upper lobe volume, small nodular increased-density opacities in the left lower lobe and right lower lobe, right pleural thickening. Following admission, two flexible bronchoscopic examinations with plastic cast removal and bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) were performed; bronchoscopic findings were consistent with plastic bronchitis and bronchial mucosal inflammation. Targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid(BALF) detected Enterovirus D68 and Rhinovirus. Intravenous immunoglobulin support and methylprednisolone anti-inflammatory therapy were also administered. By hospital day 10, the patient's condition had stabilized;Follow-up chest CT demonstrated resolution of the left upper lobe patchy high-density opacities with re-expansion of the left upper lobe, patchy high-density opacities in the left lower lobe and small left pleural effusion. The newly developed lesion in the left lower lobe was considered resolving inflammatory changes rather than new active infection. The patient was discharged with medication. At 6 days post-discharge, follow-up chest CT demonstrated complete resolution of pulmonary infiltrates, pleural effusions, consistent with full clinical recovery. The total duration of treatment was 10 days of hospitalization plus 6 days of oral therapy after discharge, giving a total of 16 days.ConclusionEV-D68 infection should be recognized as a potential etiology of plastic bronchitis or severe pneumonia in children. In addition to direct pathogen-mediated tissue injury, immune-mediated damage warrants careful consideration in the underlying pathophysiological mechanisms. Early bronchoscopic intervention combined with anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory therapy may prove critical in shortening the disease course and improving clinical outcomes.Keywords: case report, Enterovirus D68, plastic bronchitis, rhinovirus, severe pneumonia Supplementary materialThe Supplementary Material for this article can be found online at: https://www.frontiersin.org/articles/10.3389/fmed.2026.1977512/full#supplementary-material Supplementary Materials DiscussionThe case, confirmed by flexible bronchoscopy procedures with plastic cast removal and BAL were performed and BALF tNGS with detailed therapeutic documentation, provides valuable insights into the rare association between EV-D68 and plastic bronchitis in older children. This case reveals three key findings: First, EV-D68 can induce plastic bronchitis in previously healthy school-aged children,causing airway obstruction leading to respiratory distress and even respiratory failure, thereby expanding the known clinical spectrum of this infection. Evidence of airway obstruction: In this patient, chest imaging demonstrated atelectasis of the left upper lobe; bronchoscopy revealed complete or incomplete obstruction of the left main bronchus and left upper lobe bronchus lumen by plastic sputum casts; chest radiograph performed 2 days after clearance of intrabronchial casts showed re-expansion of the left upper lobe; arterial blood gas analysis indicated respiratory acidosis (elevated PaCO2 due to airway obstruction and hypoventilation) combined with metabolic acidosis (elevated lactate due to tissue hypoxia). All of the above support our argument of airway obstruction. Based on the histopathological findings in this patient, infection-related PB was considered. Second, for patients with rapidly progressive disease accompanied by hypoxemia and radiological deterioration, early bronchoscopic examination is warranted; the removal of plastic secretions and tNGS-based pathogen identification are critical for diagnosis and targeted therapy. Third, complete recovery was achieved after 16 days of comprehensive treatment incorporating repeated bronchoscopic lavage combined with intravenous immunoglobulin and methylprednisolone, suggesting that aggressive multimodal intervention may be pivotal for favorable outcomes in EV-D68–associated severe PB.In this case, histopathological examination of the plastic sputum cast revealed necrotic debris containing histiocytes, lymphocytes, eosinophils, and abundant neutrophils. Pathophysiological Mechanism of Infection-Related PB Evolution:Infection → Inflammation → Mucus Hypersecretion → Sputum Plug Formation → Fibrin Exudation → Cellular Infiltration → Cast Solidification → PB.Plastic sputum casts refer to solidified sputum plugs that form in situ within the bronchial tree, exhibiting morphological characteristics of bronchial branching architecture with dense, elastic consistency. The pathological essence represents the advanced solidified form of a mucus-inflammatory-cellular debris complex, constituting the core pathological entity of PB. Literature has demonstrated that extremely concentrated mucins (MUC5AC/MUC5B) can form gel-like solids through disulfide cross-linking without requiring a fibrin scaffold. Therefore, the currently broadly defined plastic bronchitis can be diagnosed based on the triad of “tree-like structure+mucus solidification+inflammatory cell infiltration,” with fibrin serving as supportive rather than obligatory evidence. Based on these findings, we hypothesize that EV-D68 may contribute to PB formation through the following three interconnected mechanisms(Figure 4):(1) Direct epithelial injury and impairment of mucociliary clearance: EV-D68 invades bronchial ciliated epithelium via sialic acid receptors,disrupting mucociliary function and causing mucus stasis (5–7). (2) Mucus hypersecretion: Studies have found that the EV-D68 VP3 protein interacts with mitochondrial antiviral signaling protein (MAVS) to modulate NF-κB signaling:early inhibition facilitates immune evasion,while late viral replication triggers NF-κB overactivation,upregulating MUC5AC transcription and promoting viscous mucus production that impairs mucus transport (8, 9).(3) Inflammatory cascade and cast formation: Existing studies have found that EV-D68 induces neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) through IL-17-mediated NADPH oxidase-dependent NETosis;released DNA, histones,and elastase increase mucus elasticity. Activated eosinophils degranulate cytotoxic proteins (MBP, EPX), damaging epithelium and promoting mucus plug solidification (10–14). These pathways converge to form the characteristic plastic casts of PB.Figure 4Proposed mechanisms of EV-D68-induced plastic bronchitis.Flowchart illustrating EV-D68 infection leading to plastic bronchitis. Three pathways are shown: direct epithelial injury, mucin hypersecretion, and inflammatory cascade, leading to viscous mucus, plastic cast formation, resulting in airway obstruction and severe respiratory failure.EV-D68 infection is frequently complicated by co-infection with other pathogens; synergistic inflammatory responses may promote PB development. During the 2024 outbreak in Italy, 40% of cases exhibited co-infection, while a 2014–2018 survey in Guangdong, China, found that 72.7% of cases had mixed infections, predominantly with rhinovirus, respiratory syncytial virus and bacteria (15, 16). This case identified co-infection with EV-D68 and rhinovirus. The underlying mechanisms for this co-occurrence are analyzed as follows: (a) Phylogenetic relatedness and shared tropism (17, 18): Both viruses belong to the Picornaviridae family. Moreover, EV-D68 exhibits acid lability and low-temperature growth characteristics similar to rhinovirus. full_text_sections.abstract: AbstractBackgroundPlastic bronchitis (PB) is a rare disease characterized by the formation of tree-like or tubular mucus plugs within the bronchi, which can lead to severe airway obstruction and respiratory failure, potentially becoming life-threatening if diagnosis and treatment are delayed. Enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) is a common pathogen that causes acute respiratory infections in children,which can lead to wheezing, acute flaccid myelitis, and even respiratory failure. Nevertheless, a direct association between EV-D68 infection and plastic bronchitis has not been previously reported. As the first documented case, this report establishes the association between EV-D68 and plastic bronchitis, thereby expanding the clinical spectrum of EV-D68.MethodsWe report a case of plastic bronchitis and severe pneumonia caused by Enterovirus D68 infection. To identify additional cases and elucidate the clinical characteristics of this condition, a systematic literature search was conducted using PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science databases for the period from January 2006 to June 2026. The search strategy employed the following keywords: “Enterovirus D68” “plastic bronchitis” and “severe pneumonia”.Case descriptionThis case involved an 11-year-old girl with previously good health. Chief complaints: cough and wheezing for 1 day, chest pain for half a day. Chest CT showed patchy increased-density opacities in the left upper loben with reduced left upper lobe volume, small nodular increased-density opacities in the left lower lobe and right lower lobe, right pleural thickening. Following admission, two flexible bronchoscopic examinations with plastic cast removal and bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) were performed; bronchoscopic findings were consistent with plastic bronchitis and bronchial mucosal inflammation. Targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid(BALF) detected Enterovirus D68 and Rhinovirus. Intravenous immunoglobulin support and methylprednisolone anti-inflammatory therapy were also administered. By hospital day 10, the patient's condition had stabilized;Follow-up chest CT demonstrated resolution of the left upper lobe patchy high-density opacities with re-expansion of the left upper lobe, patchy high-density opacities in the left lower lobe and small left pleural effusion. The newly developed lesion in the left lower lobe was considered resolving inflammatory changes rather than new active infection. The patient was discharged with medication. At 6 days post-discharge, follow-up chest CT demonstrated complete resolution of pulmonary infiltrates, pleural effusions, consistent with full clinical recovery. The total duration of treatment was 10 days of hospitalization plus 6 days of oral therapy after discharge, giving a total of 16 days.ConclusionEV-D68 infection should be recognized as a potential etiology of plastic bronchitis or severe pneumonia in children. In addition to direct pathogen-mediated tissue injury, immune-mediated damage warrants careful consideration in the underlying pathophysiological mechanisms. Early bronchoscopic intervention combined with anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory therapy may prove critical in shortening the disease course and improving clinical outcomes.Keywords: case report, Enterovirus D68, plastic bronchitis, rhinovirus, severe pneumonia

papers.title_original: Enterovirus D68 infection causing plastic bronchitis and severe pneumonia: a case report and literature review

analysis.scope_and_question: This review investigates the association between Enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) and plastic bronchitis in children, focusing on the clinical presentation, diagnostic methods, and treatment outcomes of a rare case. The central question is whether EV-D68 can cause plastic bronchitis and severe pneumonia, expanding the known clinical spectrum of this infection.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is based on a case report and a systematic literature search conducted using PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science databases from January 2006 to June 2026. The search strategy included the keywords 'Enterovirus D68', 'plastic bronchitis', and 'severe pneumonia'. Two flexible bronchoscopic examinations with plastic cast removal and bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) were performed, and targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) of BAL fluid detected EV-D68 and Rhinovirus.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The case report confirms that EV-D68 can induce plastic bronchitis in previously healthy school-aged children, leading to airway obstruction, respiratory distress, and even respiratory failure. The patient's condition improved with 16 days of comprehensive treatment, including repeated bronchoscopic lavage, intravenous immunoglobulin, and methylprednisolone, suggesting that aggressive multimodal intervention may be pivotal for favorable outcomes. The findings also support the argument that EV-D68 infection is a potential etiology of plastic bronchitis or severe pneumonia in children.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that while EV-D68 has been associated with acute flaccid myelitis (AFM), its potential to trigger severe lower airway disease with plastic cast formation remains underappreciated. There is no explicit mention of other related viruses like Rhinovirus being the primary cause of the condition, and the evidence is limited to a single case report. The review does not provide a comprehensive analysis of the pathophysiological mechanisms or long-term outcomes of EV-D68-associated plastic bronchitis.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The clinical significance of recognizing plastic bronchitis in the context of EV-D68 outbreaks includes the need for early bronchoscopic intervention for cast removal and airway clearance, which directly impacts survival. The inflammatory mechanisms underlying EV-D68-associated PB, particularly immune-mediated injury and eosinophilic infiltration, may inform targeted therapeutic strategies such as corticosteroids and immunoglobulin therapy. Heightened awareness among clinicians during EV-D68 epidemic seasons may facilitate timely diagnosis and reduce delays in definitive management.

analysis.summary_en: This case report and literature review explore the rare association between Enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) and plastic bronchitis in children. The study describes an 11-year-old girl with previously good health who developed plastic bronchitis and severe pneumonia, confirmed by bronchoscopy and tNGS of BAL fluid. The case highlights the clinical spectrum of EV-D68, including airway obstruction, respiratory distress, and even respiratory failure. The patient's recovery after 16 days of multimodal treatment suggests that aggressive interventions may be critical for favorable outcomes. The review emphasizes the need for early bronchoscopic examination and targeted therapies in EV-D68-associated PB, while noting that the pathophysiological mechanisms and long-term outcomes remain underexplored. The findings underscore the importance of recognizing EV-D68 as a potential cause of severe lower airway disease in children.

analysis_en.scope_and_question: This review investigates the association between Enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) and plastic bronchitis in children, focusing on the clinical presentation, diagnostic methods, and treatment outcomes of a rare case. The central question is whether EV-D68 can cause plastic bronchitis and severe pneumonia, expanding the known clinical spectrum of this infection.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is based on a case report and a systematic literature search conducted using PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science databases from January 2006 to June 2026. The search strategy included the keywords 'Enterovirus D68', 'plastic bronchitis', and 'severe pneumonia'. Two flexible bronchoscopic examinations with plastic cast removal and bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) were performed, and targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) of BAL fluid detected EV-D68 and Rhinovirus.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The case report confirms that EV-D68 can induce plastic bronchitis in previously healthy school-aged children, leading to airway obstruction, respiratory distress, and even respiratory failure. The patient's condition improved with 16 days of comprehensive treatment, including repeated bronchoscopic lavage, intravenous immunoglobulin, and methylprednisolone, suggesting that aggressive multimodal intervention may be pivotal for favorable outcomes. The findings also support the argument that EV-D68 infection is a potential etiology of plastic bronchitis or severe pneumonia in children.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that while EV-D68 has been associated with acute flaccid myelitis (AFM), its potential to trigger severe lower airway disease with plastic cast formation remains underappreciated. There is no explicit mention of other related viruses like Rhinovirus being the primary cause of the condition, and the evidence is limited to a single case report. The review does not provide a comprehensive analysis of the pathophysiological mechanisms or long-term outcomes of EV-D68-associated plastic bronchitis.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: The clinical significance of recognizing plastic bronchitis in the context of EV-D68 outbreaks includes the need for early bronchoscopic intervention for cast removal and airway clearance, which directly impacts survival. The inflammatory mechanisms underlying EV-D68-associated PB, particularly immune-mediated injury and eosinophilic infiltration, may inform targeted therapeutic strategies such as corticosteroids and immunoglobulin therapy. Heightened awareness among clinicians during EV-D68 epidemic seasons may facilitate timely diagnosis and reduce delays in definitive management.

papers.abstract: Enteroviruses are well-known causes of a wide range of infectious diseases, ranging from mild illnesses such as typical exanthema to severe conditions such as serous meningitis. Given the continued relevance of the disease, the potential for severe progression, and the lack of specific prophylaxis, epidemiological vigilance is necessary for enteroviral and its various forms. This article examines the clinical presentation of the most common forms of enteroviral infection.

papers.source_body_en: Enteroviruses are well-known causes of a wide range of infectious diseases, ranging from mild illnesses such as typical exanthema to severe conditions such as serous meningitis. Given the continued relevance of the disease, the potential for severe progression, and the lack of specific prophylaxis, epidemiological vigilance is necessary for enteroviral and its various forms. This article examines the clinical presentation of the most common forms of enteroviral infection.

papers.title: Search Strategy for a Review of the Diagnostic Landscape of Enterovirus A71 (EV-A71)
papers.abstract: This scoping review aims to map the existing evidence on the diagnostic landscape of Enterovirus A71 (EV-A71). The review aims to identify and characterise existing and emerging diagnostic approaches for EV-A71 detection, including molecular, antigen-based, and other diagnostic methods. Diagnostic performance metrics will be recorded for those commercially available and in publication. This review will identify any gaps in the diagnostic landscape and make recommendations to overcome gaps and challenges. The search strategy was developed to identify relevant literature across selected electronic databases. The complete database-specific search strings, search dates, and any applied restrictions will be documented to facilitate transparency and reproducibility. This registration provides a time-stamped record of the planned search methodology and supports the transparent conduct and reporting of the review. The protocol will be registered on the Open Science Framework (OSF) before the completion of the review. Protocol was developed March 2026 and the review is in process at the data extraction stage using Covidence.

papers.title: Đặc điểm dịch tễ học của các ca bệnh tay chân miệng nặng do Coxsackievirus A6 và đặc điểm di truyền của một số chủng tại miền Nam Việt Nam, 2022–2025 Circulation and preliminary genetic characterization of Coxsackievirus A6 causing severe hand, foot and mouth disease in southern Vietnam, 2022– 2025
papers.abstract: Coxsackievirus A6 (CV-A6) hiện là một trong những tác nhân quan trọng gây bệnh Tay Chân Miệng (TCM) phổ biến tại Việt Nam và ngày càng được ghi nhận trong các trường hợp biểu hiện bệnh nặng. Nghiên cứu này nhằm phân tích một số đặc điểm dịch tễ của các trường hợp Tay Chân Miệng nặng do CV-A6 và khảo sát đặc điểm di truyền của một số chủng CV-A6 tại miền Nam Việt Nam giai đoạn 2022–2025. Nghiên cứu được thực hiện trên các trường hợp mắc TCM thu thập trong giai đoạn 2022-2025. VRĐR và CV-A6 được phát hiện bằng kỹ thuật real-time RT-PCR. Các mẫu dương tính với CV-A6 được phân lập, giải trình tự vùng gen VP1 và phân tích phát sinh loài nhằm xác định mối quan hệ di truyền. Trong tổng số 1.974 trường hợp nghi ngờ TCM, có 1.179 trường hợp dương tính với VRĐR (59,7%), CV-A6 được phát hiện ở 83 trường hợp, tương ứng với 7% số ca dương tính với VRĐR. Nhóm nhiễm CV-A6 chủ yếu là nam giới (63,9%) và trẻ từ 1–2 tuổi (63,9%). Trong số các mẫu CV-A6 dương tính, có 4 mẫu được phân lập thành công. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to analyze the epidemiological characteristics of severe hand, foot and mouth disease (HFMD) cases caused by Coxsackievirus A6 (CV-A6) and to investigate the genetic characteristics of some CV-A6 strains in southern Vietnam from 2022 to 2025. This addresses the need to understand the epidemiology and genetic diversity of CV-A6, which is a significant cause of HFMD in Vietnam.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted on HFMD cases collected from 2022 to 2025 in southern Vietnam. The design involved real-time RT-PCR for virus detection and sequencing of the VP1 region to determine genetic characteristics.
analysis.methods: HFMD cases were identified using real-time RT-PCR, and successful isolation and sequencing of the VP1 region were performed on positive samples to analyze genetic diversity.
analysis.main_results: Out of 1,974 suspected HFMD cases, 1,179 (59.7%) were positive for viral RNA (VR), and CV-A6 was detected in 83 cases (7% of VR-positive cases). The infection was predominantly in male children aged 1-2 years.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study identified the presence of CV-A6 in severe HFMD cases and found that all sequenced strains belonged to the D3c sublineage of the D3 lineage, providing evidence of the circulation of D3c in southern Vietnam during the study period.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the importance of continuous molecular epidemiological surveillance to monitor the evolution and circulation of enteroviruses, which can inform scientific and public health strategies for HFMD prevention and control.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the sample size and the fact that only a subset of positive samples were sequenced. The evidence strength is moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed the epidemiological characteristics and genetic diversity of Coxsackievirus A6 (CV-A6) causing severe hand, foot and mouth disease (HFMD) in southern Vietnam from 2022 to 2025. Out of 1,974 suspected cases, 83 (7%) were positive for CV-A6, with infections predominantly in young male children. Sequencing showed all strains belonged to the D3c sublineage, indicating the circulation of this strain in the region.

analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the importance of continuous molecular epidemiological surveillance to monitor the evolution and circulation of enteroviruses, which can inform scientific and public health strategies for HFMD prevention and control.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the sample size and the fact that only a subset of positive samples were sequenced. The evidence strength is moderate due to these limitations.

papers.title_zh: 柯萨奇病毒 A6 病毒与柯萨奇病毒 A6 相关chủng tại miền Nam Việt Nam,2022-2025 导致越南南部严重手足口病的柯萨奇病毒 A6 的传播和初步遗传特征,2022-2025
papers.source_body_en: Coxsackievirus A6 (CV-A6) hiện là một trong những tác nhân quan trọng gây bệnh Tay Chân Miệng (TCM) phổ biến tại Việt Nam và ngày càng được ghi nhận trong các trường hợp biểu hiện bệnh nặng. Nghiên cứu này nhằm phân tích một số đặc điểm dịch tễ của các trường hợp Tay Chân Miệng nặng do CV-A6 và khảo sát đặc điểm di truyền của một số chủng CV-A6 tại miền Nam Việt Nam giai đoạn 2022–2025. Nghiên cứu được thực hiện trên các trường hợp mắc TCM thu thập trong giai đoạn 2022-2025. VRĐR và CV-A6 được phát hiện bằng kỹ thuật real-time RT-PCR. Các mẫu dương tính với CV-A6 được phân lập, giải trình tự vùng gen VP1 và phân tích phát sinh loài nhằm xác định mối quan hệ di truyền. Trong tổng số 1.974 trường hợp nghi ngờ TCM, có 1.179 trường hợp dương tính với VRĐR (59,7%), CV-A6 được phát hiện ở 83 trường hợp, tương ứng với 7% số ca dương tính với VRĐR. Nhóm nhiễm CV-A6 chủ yếu là nam giới (63,9%) và trẻ từ 1–2 tuổi (63,9%). Trong số các mẫu CV-A6 dương tính, có 4 mẫu được phân lập thành công. Kết quả giải trình tự vùng gen VP1 cho thấy tất cả các chủng đều thuộc phân nhánh D3c của dòng D3. Đây là bằng chứng về sự hiện diện của phân nhánh D3c trong các trường hợp TCM nặng tại miền Nam Việt Nam giai đoạn 2022–2025. Kết quả nhấn mạnh vai trò của giám sát dịch tễ học phân tử liên tục nhằm theo dõi sự tiến hóa và lưu hành của VRĐR, góp phần cung cấp cơ sở khoa học cho công tác phòng và kiểm soát TCM.

papers.title: Evaluating the antiviral effects of polygonum cuspidatum nanoparticles against enterovirus 71 in vitro and in vivo.
papers.abstract: Enterovirus 71 (EV71) is a major causative agent of hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) and is associated with severe neurological complications in young children. However, effective antiviral therapeutics remain limited. In this study, nanoparticles derived from Polygonum cuspidatum (NPC) were prepared and their antiviral activity against EV71 was evaluated in vitro and in vivo. Cytotoxicity and antiviral assays in human rhabdomyosarcoma (RD) cells demonstrated that NPC exhibited substantially lower cytotoxicity than the crude extract while maintaining comparable antiviral potency against EV71. NPC treatment markedly reduced EV71-induced cytopathic effects and significantly decreased viral RNA levels, as confirmed by indirect immunofluorescence and RT-qPCR. In an EV71-infected ICR suckling mouse model, oral administration of NPC significantly improved survival, attenuated clinical disease scores and body weight loss, and reduced viral loads in muscle and brain tissues in a dose-dependent manner. Histopathological analysis revealed alleviated tissue injury in the NPC-treated mice. These findings suggest that nanonization improves the therapeutic index of P. cuspidatum and support further investigation of NPC as a potential plant-derived antiviral candidate for EV71 infection.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估虎杖纳米颗粒 (NPC) 对肠道病毒 71 (EV71) 的 抗病毒药物 作用,肠道病毒是手足口病 (HFMD) 的主要病原体,并与幼儿严重的神经系统并发症相关。有效的 抗病毒药物 疗法仍然有限。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用人横纹肌肉瘤 (RD) 细胞在体外评估了 NPC 对抗 EV71 的 抗病毒药物 活性,并使用感染 EV71 的 ICR 乳鼠模型在体内评估了 NPC 对抗 EV71 的 抗病毒药物 活性。
elements_zh.methods: 制备 NPC,并通过 RD 细胞和 EV71 感染的 ICR 乳鼠模型中的细胞毒性和 抗病毒药物 测定来评估其 抗病毒药物 活性。
elements_zh.main_results: NPC 表现出比粗提物更低的细胞毒性,同时保持与 抗病毒药物 相当的针对 EV71 的效力。在体内,NPC 治疗 以剂量依赖的方式提高了生存率,减轻了临床疾病评分,减少了体重减轻,并降低了肌肉和脑组织中的病毒载量。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现表明,纳米化提高了虎杖的治疗指数,并支持进一步研究 NPC 作为 EV71 感染的潜在植物源 抗病毒药物 候选药物。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,NPC 可能是治疗 EV71 感染的有前景的 抗病毒药物 候选药物,有可能改善 治疗 的结果并减少幼儿的严重神经系统并发症。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性包括使用单一动物模型以及需要进一步研究以证实人体临床试验的结果。由于样本量有限且需要重复,证据强度中等。

papers.title: Transcriptome analysis of mRNA and long non-coding RNA profiles in the brains of CVA10-infected suckling mice.
papers.abstract: Hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) caused by Coxsackievirus A10 (CVA10) remains an important public health concern. Although most infections are self-limiting, severe cases may develop neurological complications, including acute flaccid paralysis and aseptic meningitis. However, host transcriptional responses to CVA10 infection within the central nervous system (CNS) remain poorly understood. Here, we established a CVA10-infected ICR suckling mouse model and performed transcriptomic profiling of brain tissues using RNA-seq, followed by RT-qPCR validation. A total of 243 differentially expressed mRNAs and 776 differentially expressed lncRNAs were identified in the brains of CVA10-infected mice. Interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) such as Ifit1 exhibited significant dysregulation in CVA10-infected brain tissue. Integrated GO and KEGG functional enrichment analyses revealed that these genes were significantly associated with innate immune and inflammatory responses, particularly interferon-related signaling pathways. Protein–protein interaction network analysis identified ten immune-related hub genes, including Irf7 , Rsad2 , Isg15 , Stat1 , Ifih1 , Ifit1 , Ifit3 , Oasl2 , Rtp4 and Usp18 . RT-qPCR validation showed overall agreement with RNA-seq findings, supporting the reliability of the transcriptomic analysis. Long non coding RNAs can extensively regulate these immune-related genes in both directions. These results offer a foundation for further investigation of the molecular basis of CVA10-related neurological disease, and for exploring candidate biomarkers and molecular targets.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the host transcriptional response to Coxsackievirus A10 (CVA10) infection in the central nervous system (CNS) of suckling mice. The research aimed to understand the molecular mechanisms underlying CVA10-related neurological complications, such as acute flaccid paralysis and aseptic meningitis. Using RNA-seq and RT-qPCR, the study identified 243 differentially expressed mRNAs and 776 lncRNAs, with significant dysregulation of interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) like Ifit1. Functional enrichment analyses revealed associations with innate immune and inflammatory responses, particularly interferon-related pathways. The results highlight the potential role of long non-coding RNAs in regulating immune-related genes and provide a foundation for future research on CVA10's pathogenesis and therapeutic targets. However, the study is limited to an animal model and does not include human data, which may affect the generalizability of findings.

papers.title: Hand, Foot, and Mouth Disease with Probable Intrafamilial Transmission in a 15-Month-Old Infant: A Case Report
papers.abstract: Hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) is an acute exanthema disease caused by a viral infection which is generally self-limiting, most often caused by Coxsackievirus A16 and Enterovirus 71, and more often attacks children under five years of age. Problem: Transmission within the family through direct contact with secretions or lesion fluid from infected individuals is a recognized transmission route, however case reports that specifically state the possibility of intrafamilial transmission in children under two years old are still rare in the literature. Case report: We report a case of HFMD in a 15 month old boy who was brought to the outpatient facility with complaints of reddish rashes around the mouth, hands and feet since two days previously, preceded by fever as a prodromal symptom. Physical examination showed maculopapular and vesicular lesions in the perioral region, right wrist, and bilateral lower extremities, with generalized distribution and miliary to lenticular size. A history of close contact with an older sibling who experienced similar symptoms approximately one week previously supports the possibility of intrafamilial transmission between siblings. Management: The diagnosis is made clinically without laboratory supporting examinations. The patient received supportive treatment in the form of paracetamol syrup, 2% mupirocin ointment, and immunostimulants, accompanied by education to parents regarding hand hygiene and isolating the patient from other family members. Conclusion: This case emphasizes the importance of a systematic history of intrafamilial contact history in children with suspected HFMD, as well as the need for targeted family education to break the chain of transmission in the household environment.

papers.title_zh: 15 个月大婴儿可能患有家族内 传播 的手足口病:A 病例报告
papers.source_body_en: Hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) is an acute exanthema disease caused by a viral infection which is generally self-limiting, most often caused by Coxsackievirus A16 and Enterovirus 71, and more often attacks children under five years of age. Problem: Transmission within the family through direct contact with secretions or lesion fluid from infected individuals is a recognized transmission route, however case reports that specifically state the possibility of intrafamilial transmission in children under two years old are still rare in the literature. Case report: We report a case of HFMD in a 15 month old boy who was brought to the outpatient facility with complaints of reddish rashes around the mouth, hands and feet since two days previously, preceded by fever as a prodromal symptom. Physical examination showed maculopapular and vesicular lesions in the perioral region, right wrist, and bilateral lower extremities, with generalized distribution and miliary to lenticular size. A history of close contact with an older sibling who experienced similar symptoms approximately one week previously supports the possibility of intrafamilial transmission between siblings. Management: The diagnosis is made clinically without laboratory supporting examinations. The patient received supportive treatment in the form of paracetamol syrup, 2% mupirocin ointment, and immunostimulants, accompanied by education to parents regarding hand hygiene and isolating the patient from other family members. Conclusion: This case emphasizes the importance of a systematic history of intrafamilial contact history in children with suspected HFMD, as well as the need for targeted family education to break the chain of transmission in the household environment.
papers.abstract_zh: 手足口病(HFMD)是一种由病毒感染引起的急性出疹性疾病,通常具有自限性,最常见的是由柯萨奇病毒 A16 和肠道病毒 71 引起,更常见于 5 岁以下儿童。问题:通过直接接触感染者的分泌物或病变液体在家庭内传播传播是公认的传播途径,但是专门说明两岁以下儿童家庭内传播可能性的传播文献仍然很少。病例报告:我们报告了一名 15 个月大男孩的手足口病病例,他被带到门诊机构,自两天前起,主诉口腔、手和脚周围出现微红色皮疹,随后出现发烧作为前驱症状。体格检查发现口周、右腕及双侧下肢有斑丘疹和水疱性病变,分布广泛,大小为粟粒状至晶状体。与大约一周前经历过类似症状的年长兄弟姐妹的密切接触史支持兄弟姐妹之间存在家庭内 传播 的可能性。管理:诊断是临床制作的,没有实验室支持检查。患者接受了对乙酰氨基酚糖浆、2%莫匹罗星软膏和免疫增强剂形式的支持性 治疗,同时向家长进行了有关手部卫生的教育,并将患者与其他家庭成员隔离。结论:该病例强调了疑似手足口病儿童系统性家庭内接触史的重要性,以及有针对性的家庭教育打破家庭环境中“传播”链条的必要性。

news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Saturday, October 31, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Biology How Enterovirus A71 Reaches the Brain: A Multistage Model of Neuroinvasion by October 28, 2026 in Biology Reading Time: 3 mins read 0 How Enterovirus A71 Reaches the Brain: A Multistage Model of Neuroinvasion Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Enterovirus A71, a virus best known for causing hand, foot, and mouth disease in children, occasionally produces severe neurological complications, yet most infections remain confined to peripheral sites. A new review article in Frontiers in Microbiology argues that this striking disparity can only be understood by treating EV-A71 neuropathogenesis as a multistage process rather than a single event. The authors, led by YZ Yi Zhang of Zunyi Medical University, propose that progression to severe disease requires the virus to overcome distinct constraints at each successive stage, from peripheral replication through systemic dissemination, central nervous system entry, establishment of productive CNS infection, and ultimately tissue injury. The review emphasizes that these stages are mechanistically connected but not interchangeable. Crossing the blood-brain barrier, for example, is not synonymous with disrupting it, and gaining entry to the central nervous system does not necessarily lead to productive infection there. According to the authors, current evidence supports two routes of CNS entry: a neurovascular route across the blood-brain barrier and a peripheral neural route along nerves. The strength of the supporting evidence, however, differs markedly between the two. Human-derived blood-brain barrier models demonstrate that EV-A71 and virus-associated carriers can engage and cross neurovascular interfaces, establishing mechanistic feasibility for the vascular route. Discover more Check Symptoms Find Neurologists Try Brain Games Study Anatomy Find Treatments For the peripheral neural route, the evidence base is described as more causally robust. Temporal studies in animals, perturbation of axonal transport, and compartmentalized neuronal models together provide stronger causal support for retrograde axonal transport, the process by which the virus travels backward along nerve fibers toward the central nervous system once it has accessed peripheral nerves. Despite this mechanistic progress, the review is explicit about what remains unknown. The timing, necessity, and relative contribution of each route during natural infection in children remain unresolved. Animal models and in vitro systems can demonstrate what is possible, but they cannot by themselves establish what actually happens in the course of human infection, where the interplay of viral properties, host factors, and tissue context may differ substantially. To organize these observations, the authors propose a multistage progression-constraint model. In this framework, progression to severe neurological disease requires EV-A71 to overcome distinct barriers imposed by tissue context, viral properties, and host factors at successive stages. Most infections fail at one of these constraints and remain peripheral, while only a minority of viruses successfully navigate every stage and produce CNS disease. The model is presented as a testable explanation rather than a settled conclusion, and it generates specific questions about where in the sequence most infections are stopped. The framework also highlights the need for longitudinal clinical studies that follow infected children over time, as well as directly comparable experimental models that allow findings from different laboratories to be aligned. Without such comparability, the authors suggest, the field will struggle to identify the precise point at which disease trajectories diverge, which is arguably the most clinically important question in EV-A71 neuropathogenesis. Discover more Study Biology infections neurological disease neurological Uninterruptible power supplies The review was received on 1 September 2026 and accepted on 12 October 2026, and its final formatted version is pending publication. It was authored by researchers at Zunyi Medical University, its affiliated hospital, and Zunyi Medical and Pharmaceutical College, with correspondence attributed to Bo Huang and Zhenzhuang Zou. For clinicians and researchers, the central message is one of caution and structure. EV-A71 remains an important cause of severe neurological complications of hand, foot, and mouth disease in children, and understanding why only a small proportion of infections progress to CNS disease requires disentangling entry, establishment, and injury as separate events. The multistage constraint model offers a roadmap for that effort, while the authors themselves stress that the mechanisms underlying the transition from peripheral infection to neurological disease remain incompletely understood and demand further study. analysis.brief_en: A review article published on October 28, 2026, by Bioengineer.org explores the mechanisms by which Enterovirus A71 (EV-A71) reaches the brain, proposing a multistage model of neuroinvasion. The study, led by researchers at Zunyi Medical University, highlights that EV-A71, known for causing hand, foot, and mouth disease in children, can lead to severe neurological complications. The authors argue that progression to CNS disease involves overcoming distinct constraints at each stage, from peripheral replication to tissue injury. While two routes of CNS entry are identified—neurovascular across the blood-brain barrier and peripheral neural along nerves—the evidence for each differs. The vascular route is supported by human-derived blood-brain barrier models, while the neural route is backed by animal studies and in vitro systems. However, the exact timing, necessity, and relative contribution of these routes during natural infection in children remain unresolved. The review underscores the importance of longitudinal clinical studies and comparable experimental models to better understand the transition from peripheral infection to neurological disease. It is presented as a framework for future research rather than a definitive conclusion.

news.content_zh: Bioengineer.org 于 2026 年 10 月 28 日发表的一篇评论文章探讨了肠道病毒 A71 (EV-A71) 到达大脑的机制,提出了神经侵袭的多阶段模型。这项由遵义医科大学研究人员领导的研究强调,以引起儿童手足口病而闻名的 EV-A71 可导致严重的神经并发症。作者认为,中枢神经系统疾病的进展涉及克服每个阶段的不同限制,从外周复制到组织损伤。虽然已经确定了两种进入中枢神经系统的途径——穿过血脑屏障的神经血管和沿着神经的周围神经——但每种途径的证据都不同。血管途径得到人源血脑屏障模型的支持,而神经途径得到动物研究和体外系统的支持。然而,这些途径在儿童自然感染过程中的确切时间、必要性和相对贡献仍未解决。该综述强调了纵向临床研究和可比实验模型的重要性,以更好地了解从外周感染到神经系统疾病的转变。它是作为未来研究的框架而不是明确的结论。

Despite decades of research, no virus-specific therapy against this broad group of pathogens has been approved by regulatory agencies, leaving clinicians to manage infections ranging from mild respiratory illness to myocarditis, encephalitis and acute flaccid myelitis with supportive care alone. A new computational study published in BMC Methods now reports a detailed molecular modelling campaign on novel derivatives of pleconaril, one of the most extensively studied capsid-binding antienteroviral candidates, in an effort to identify promising lead compounds for future drug development. The research, led by Chetan Palvi, Snehal Ukhade, Isha S. Ingle and Hemchandra K. Chaudhari with Sanchali S. Gadade, assembled a ligand library of twenty-four novel pleconaril derivatives drawn from the literature, each with reported antienteroviral activity. Using the PHASE module of the Schrödinger modelling suite, the team built atom-based and field-based three-dimensional quantitative structure-activity relationship (3D-QSAR) models, generated a common pharmacophore hypothesis, docked every compound into the capsid protein of enterovirus D68 and estimated binding free energies with the MM/GBSA method. Molecular properties and absorption, distribution, metabolism and excretion parameters were assessed with the QikProp utility and SwissADME. The biological target was chosen with care. The crystal structure of human enterovirus D68 in complex with pleconaril, deposited in the Protein Data Bank under the identifier 4WM7, was resolved at 2.32 angstroms and imported into Maestro for preparation. Bound ligands, cofactors and water molecules were removed, side chains that did not participate in the binding cavity were neutralised with the OPLS_2005 force field, and hydrogen atoms were added. The quality of the prepared structure was checked with a Ramachandran plot before docking grids were generated around the centroid of the co-crystallised ligand. Enteroviruses belong to the Enterovirus genus of the Picornaviridae family and comprise roughly one hundred serotypes across species A to D. This diversity is a major obstacle to vaccination: the only vaccines currently available target poliomyelitis caused by polioviruses, two inactivated enterovirus A71 vaccines used in China against hand-foot-and-mouth disease, and a vaccine against the foot-and-mouth disease virus of livestock. Small molecules that attack conserved steps of the viral life cycle therefore address a significant unmet clinical need, and the capsid’s hydrophobic pocket has long been viewed as an attractive point of attack. That pocket normally holds a fatty acid known as the pocket factor, which is expelled when the virus attaches to a host cell. The resulting conformational changes in the capsid facilitate the release of the viral genomic RNA. Capsid-binding inhibitors compete with the pocket factor for occupancy of the hydrophobic cavity and can block viral attachment or uncoating. Pleconaril, vapendavir and pocapavir are among the most extensively studied candidates exploiting this mechanism, yet none has reached clinical approval, which is precisely why the authors focused their modelling effort on pleconaril analogues. The clinical setbacks in this drug class are instructive. Pleconaril was not approved by the US Food and Drug Administration for treating the common cold because of adverse effects including headache, diarrhoea and nausea, its induction of the cytochrome P-450 enzyme CYP3A4, which accelerates the metabolism of ethinyl estradiol, and the emergence of pleconaril-resistant viruses. In February 2017, vapendavir failed in a phase IIb trial owing to insufficient efficacy against rhinoviruses compared with placebo. In a randomised, blinded, placebo-controlled study of poliovirus-infected patients treated with pocapavir, resistance was recorded in 44 percent of the treated group versus 10 percent of the placebo group. Developing effective, selective and broad-spectrum antienteroviral agents remains a key focus for medicinal chemists. Against this backdrop, the docking results provide the study’s headline numbers. The 12b complex with 4WM7 also yielded a favourable Prime MM/GBSA binding free energy of minus 111.54 kilocalories per mole, which the authors report as superior to the complexes formed with the reference standards. Structural analysis of the docked poses indicated pi-pi stacking interactions between the isoxazole ring of the derivatives and the residue TYR193 within the binding site. Validation of the docking protocol was built into the workflow. The co-crystallised native ligand was re-docked into its binding site, and the resulting root-mean-square-deviation values of less than 2 angstroms confirmed that the procedure reproduced the experimentally observed binding mode. Scoring was performed in Glide’s Extra Precision mode, and all twenty-four compounds were allowed to dock into the same cavity. Swiss Target Prediction was then applied to the best-docked molecule, 12b, suggesting probable engagement of four target families: kinases at 60 percent, enzymes at 13.3 percent, and G-protein coupled receptors and proteases at 6.7 percent each. The pharmacophore work distilled the activity data into a spatial template. Ligands with a pIC50 value above 6.3 were classed as active and those below as inactive, yielding seventeen active and seven inactive compounds. Twenty hypotheses were generated, and the top-ranked six-point model, designated AHHRRR_1, was selected on the basis of a site score of 0.917, a phase hyposcore of 1.337 and a survival score of 5.610. The model combines one hydrogen bond acceptor feature, two hydrophobic features and three aromatic ring features, and every active compound in the dataset could be aligned onto it, offering a blueprint for designing future analogues. Leave-one-out cross-validation was used to assess stability and robustness, while RMSE, Q2 and Pearson’s r values for the test set quantified predictive power. The contour maps localise the structure-activity signals: blue cubes around the 5-amidoisoxazole moiety suggest that electron-withdrawing capability there may benefit activity, whereas red cubes over the pyridine region warn that further electron-withdrawing substitution could hinder it. In the field-based maps, a favoured electropositive zone surrounds the carboxylic portion attached to the isoxazole ring, a favourable steric region encircles the pyridine ring, and hydrophobic substitution near the pyridine core correlates with intermediate activity. The ADME screening added a drug-like filter to the computational picture. QikProp calculations showed that all compounds, with a few exceptions, fell within reasonable ranges for molecular properties, the rule-of-five values lay within acceptable limits, and the predicted percentage of human oral absorption exceeded 85 percent for most molecules. One outlier illustrates the practical limits of such predictions: molecule 12c, the weakest docked compound, contains an ester and an imine that can hydrolyse at high or low pH, so QikProp could not produce data for it, and the profile of the second-to-last molecule, 19, was reported instead. The authors are careful to frame the work as computational hypothesis generation rather than proof of therapeutic value. Docking scores, MM/GBSA energies and QSAR statistics rank and rationalise compounds against a single crystal structure; they do not demonstrate antiviral efficacy in infected cells, animals or patients, and the twenty-four-compound dataset is modest by QSAR standards. The value of the study lies in the tools it leaves behind: validated atom-based and field-based 3D-QSAR models, a six-point pharmacophore that all active ligands satisfy, and a comparative docking map of the capsid pocket that together could guide the design of the next generation of pleconaril derivatives as candidate antienteroviral medicines. analysis.time: The study was published on October 29, 2026, with the event date being February 2017 for the vapendavir trial.
analysis.location_and_population: The research was conducted in the context of human enterovirus studies, with specific mention of enterovirus D68 and its capsid structure.
analysis.event: A computational study published in BMC Methods investigated pleconaril derivatives as potential antienteroviral agents, focusing on their interaction with the capsid protein of enterovirus D68.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The study identified 17 active and 7 inactive pleconaril derivatives based on pIC50 values. It also noted resistance issues in previous trials, such as 44% resistance in pocapavir-treated poliovirus patients.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study used computational models and docking simulations to evaluate the derivatives. Validation was performed using cross-validation and RMSD values, and the results are based on molecular properties and pharmacophore analysis.

analysis.brief_en: A computational study published in BMC Methods on October 29, 2026, investigated pleconaril derivatives as potential antienteroviral agents, specifically targeting the capsid protein of enterovirus D68. The research, led by Chetan Palvi and colleagues, built 3D-QSAR models and docked compounds into the virus's hydrophobic pocket, a known site for capsid-binding inhibitors. The study reported that 17 out of 24 derivatives had pIC50 values above 6.3, indicating antienteroviral activity. It also highlighted challenges in drug development, such as resistance observed in previous trials with pocapavir and vapendavir. The findings suggest a blueprint for designing future analogues, with the top-ranked model AHHRRR_1 showing strong alignment with active compounds. The research underscores the need for effective, broad-spectrum antienteroviral agents due to the diversity of enterovirus serotypes and the lack of approved therapies. The study's results are based on molecular modeling and pharmacophore analysis, with validation through cross-validation and RMSD checks.
